subject: math
title: Grade 5 Benchmarks and Estimation
seo_title: Grade 5 Benchmarks and Estimation Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on benchmarks and estimation for the BC curriculum: round whole numbers to 1 000 000, use the fraction benchmarks 0, 1/2 and 1 and the decimal benchmarks 0, 0.5 and 1, estimate sums and products, and check if answers are reasonable. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Compare with a friendly number: 0, 1/2 or 1 for fractions, 0, 0.5 or 1 for decimals.
key_sub: 3/8 is closest to 1/2 (3 is close to half of 8), and 0.09 is closest to 0. To estimate, round first: 48 × 31 is about 50 × 30 = 1500. If an answer is far from the estimate, check it.
body_html:
What is a benchmark?

A benchmark is a friendly number you can compare with, like 0, 1, 12, 0.5 or 500 000. Benchmarks help you estimate: find a quick answer that is close to the exact answer.

Whole numbers: round to a benchmark

Look at the digit one place to the right of the place you are rounding to. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down. Exactly halfway rounds up.

Round to the nearestLook at theExample
thousandhundreds digit58 702 → 59 000
ten thousandthousands digit73 150 → 70 000
hundred thousandten thousands digit651 200 → 700 000
Do not round in steps

Round 348 500 to the nearest hundred thousand.

Look only at the ten thousands digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. (Rounding in steps, 348 500 → 350 000 → 400 000, gives the wrong answer.)

Answer: 300 000

Fractions: 0, 12 or 1?

Compare the top number with the bottom number. If the top is about half of the bottom, the fraction is close to 12. If the top is small, it is close to 0. If the top is almost the same as the bottom, it is close to 1.

Estimate a fraction sum

Estimate 78 + 49.

78 is close to 1. 49 is close to 12. 1 + 12 = 112.

Answer: about 112

Decimals: 0, 0.5 or 1?

0.5 is the same as 0.50 and 0.500. Write the decimals with the same number of places, then compare.

Round with 0.5

Round 3.48 to the nearest whole number.

The decimal part is 0.48. 0.48 is less than 0.50, so round down. (Do not look only at the 8.)

Answer: 3

Estimate sums and products

Round each number, then add or multiply in your head. For products, round each number to its greatest place, multiply the front digits and then write the zeros.

Estimate a product

Estimate 48 × 31.

Round: 50 × 30. 5 × 3 = 15, then write 2 zeros: 1500. (The exact answer is 1488.)

Answer: about 1500

Is the answer reasonable?

Liam says 375 × 28 = 1050.

Estimate: 400 × 30 = 12 000. 1050 is far from 12 000, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 10 500.

Answer: not reasonable

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
“38 is closest to 1 because 8 is big.”Compare 3 with half of 8 (4): 38 is closest to 12
“0.09 is close to 1 because 9 is big.”0.09 is 9 hundredths: it is closest to 0
Rounding the wrong place: 63 820 to the nearest ten thousand → 64 000Look at the thousands digit: 3, so 60 000
Rounding in steps: 348 500 → 350 000 → 400 000Look only at the ten thousands digit: 4, so 300 000
Losing a zero: 50 × 30 = 1505 × 3 = 15, then write both zeros: 1500

faq.q: What are benchmarks in Grade 5 math in BC?
faq.a: Benchmarks are friendly numbers used to compare and estimate. In the BC Grade 5 curriculum, students use whole-number benchmarks like 500 000, the fraction benchmarks 0, 1/2 and 1, and the decimal benchmarks 0, 0.5 and 1.

faq.q: How do you tell if a fraction is closer to 0, 1/2 or 1?
faq.a: Compare the top number with half of the bottom number. 3/8 is close to 1/2 because 3 is close to 4 (half of 8), while 1/8 is close to 0 and 7/8 is close to 1.

faq.q: How do you estimate a product like 48 × 31?
faq.a: Round each number to its greatest place: 50 × 30. Multiply 5 × 3 = 15 and write the two zeros, so the estimate is 1500 (the exact answer is 1488).

faq.q: How can my child check if an answer is reasonable?
faq.a: Estimate first, then compare. If 375 × 28 gives 1050 but 400 × 30 = 12 000, the answer is far too small and should be checked.

items.q: Round 23 486 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: 23 486 is between 23 000 and 24 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in steps (23 486 → 23 490 → 23 500 → 24 000). Look only at the hundreds digit. Answer: 23 000.

items.q: Round 58 702 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: 58 702 is between 58 000 and 59 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 7. 7 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 59 000.

items.q: Round 129 650 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: 129 650 is between 129 000 and 130 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 130 000.

items.q: Round 46 820 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: 46 820 is between 40 000 and 50 000. Look at the thousands digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 50 000.

items.q: Round 73 150 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: 73 150 is between 70 000 and 80 000. Look at the thousands digit: 3. 3 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 70 000.

items.q: Round 85 000 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: 85 000 is exactly halfway between 80 000 and 90 000. The thousands digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 90 000.

items.q: Round 196 400 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: 196 400 is between 190 000 and 200 000. Look at the thousands digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 200 000.

items.q: Round 284 615 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: 284 615 is between 280 000 and 290 000. Look at the thousands digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in steps (284 615 → 284 620 → 284 600 → 285 000 → 290 000). Look only at the thousands digit. Answer: 280 000.

items.q: Round 651 200 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: 651 200 is between 600 000 and 700 000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 5. 5 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 700 000.

items.q: Round 348 500 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: 348 500 is between 300 000 and 400 000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in steps (348 500 → 349 000 → 350 000 → 400 000). Look only at the ten thousands digit. Answer: 300 000.

items.q: Round 450 000 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: 450 000 is exactly halfway between 400 000 and 500 000. The ten thousands digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 500 000.

items.q: Round 962 400 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: 962 400 is between 900 000 and 1 000 000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 1 000 000.

items.q: Round 37 951 to the nearest hundred.
items.e: 37 951 is between 37 900 and 38 000. Look at the tens digit: 5. 5 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 38 000.

items.q: Round 507 380 to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: 507 380 is between 500 000 and 600 000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 0. 0 is 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 500 000.

items.q: The dot shows 742 000. Which benchmark is it closest to: 0, 250 000, 500 000, 750 000 or 1 000 000?
items.e: 742 000 is only 8000 from 750 000. It is 242 000 from 500 000 and 258 000 from 1 000 000. Closest benchmark: 750 000.

items.q: The dot shows 281 000. Which benchmark is it closest to: 0, 250 000, 500 000, 750 000 or 1 000 000?
items.e: 281 000 is only 31 000 from 250 000. It is 219 000 from 500 000 and 281 000 from 0. Closest benchmark: 250 000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 60 000 when you round to the nearest ten thousand?
items.e: Round each one: 55 300 → 60 000; 54 990 → 50 000 (the thousands digit is 4); 65 000 → 70 000 (exactly halfway rounds up); 66 100 → 70 000. Only 55 300 rounds to 60 000.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 400 000 when you round to the nearest hundred thousand?
items.e: The numbers from 350 000 to 449 999 round to 400 000. 349 999 has a 4 in the ten thousands place, so it rounds down to 300 000. The smallest is 350 000.

items.q: Which digit do you look at to round 463 815 to the nearest ten thousand?
items.e: To round to the nearest ten thousand, look one place to the right of the ten thousands: the thousands digit, 3. 3 is 4 or less, so 463 815 rounds down to 460 000.

items.q: Owen rounds 63 820 to the nearest ten thousand and gets 64 000. What should he get?
items.e: Owen rounded to the nearest thousand. For the nearest ten thousand, look at the thousands digit: 3. 3 is 4 or less, so round down. 63 820 rounds to 60 000.

items.q: The dot shows 18. Which benchmark is 18 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 18 is 18 from 0, 38 from 12 and 78 from 1. It is closest to 0.

items.q: The dot shows 78. Which benchmark is 78 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 78 is 78 from 0, 38 from 12 and 18 from 1. It is closest to 1.

items.q: The dot shows 58. Which benchmark is 58 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 58 is 58 from 0, 18 from 12 and 38 from 1. It is closest to 12. Tip: half of 8 is 4, and 5 is close to 4.

items.q: Which benchmark is 110 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 110 is 110 from 0, 25 from 12 and 910 from 1. It is closest to 0.

items.q: Which benchmark is 910 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 910 is 910 from 0, 25 from 12 and 110 from 1. It is closest to 1.

items.q: Which benchmark is 410 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 410 is 25 from 0, 110 from 12 and 35 from 1. It is closest to 12. Tip: half of 10 is 5, and 4 is close to 5.

items.q: Which benchmark is 56 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 56 is 56 from 0, 13 from 12 and 16 from 1. It is closest to 1.

items.q: Which benchmark is 16 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 16 is 16 from 0, 13 from 12 and 56 from 1. It is closest to 0.

items.q: Which benchmark is 712 closest to: 0, 12 or 1?
items.e: 712 is 712 from 0, 112 from 12 and 512 from 1. It is closest to 12. Tip: half of 12 is 6, and 7 is close to 6.

items.q: Ava says 38 is closest to 1 because 8 is a big number. Is she right?
c: No, it is exactly 12
No, it is closest to 12
items.e: Ava is not right. A big bottom number means small parts. 38 is 38 from 0, 18 from 12 and 58 from 1. Half of 8 is 4, and 3 is close to 4, so 38 is closest to 12.

items.q: Which fraction is closest to 1?
items.e: Find how far each one is from 1: 1112 is 112 away; 34 is 14 away; 512 is 712 away; 112 is 1112 away. 1112 is the closest.

items.q: Which fraction is closest to 0?
items.e: Find how far each one is from 0: 29 is 29 away; 13 is 13 away; 59 is 59 away; 89 is 89 away. 29 is the closest.

items.q: Compare 37 and 59. Which statement is true?
c: 37 > 59
37 < 59
37 = 59
items.e: Use 12 as a benchmark. Double the top: 2 × 3 = 6, which is less than 7, so 37 is less than 12. Double the top: 2 × 5 = 10, which is more than 9, so 59 is more than 12. So 37 < 59.

items.q: Compare 78 and 49. Which statement is true?
c: 78 < 49
78 > 49
78 = 49
items.e: Use 12 as a benchmark. Double the top: 2 × 7 = 14, which is more than 8, so 78 is more than 12. Double the top: 2 × 4 = 8, which is less than 9, so 49 is less than 12. So 78 > 49.

items.q: Use the benchmarks 0, 12 and 1 to estimate 49 + 110.
items.e: 49 is close to 12 and 110 is close to 0. 12 + 0 = 12. Do not add the tops and the bottoms: the answer is not 519.

items.q: Use the benchmarks 0, 12 and 1 to estimate 78 + 110.
items.e: 78 is close to 1 and 110 is close to 0. 1 + 0 = 1. Do not add the tops and the bottoms: the answer is not 818.

items.q: Use the benchmarks 0, 12 and 1 to estimate 56 + 49.
items.e: 56 is close to 1 and 49 is close to 12. 1 + 12 = 112. Do not add the tops and the bottoms: the answer is not 915.

items.q: Use the benchmarks 0, 12 and 1 to estimate 910 + 1112.
items.e: 910 is close to 1 and 1112 is close to 1. 1 + 1 = 2. Do not add the tops and the bottoms: the answer is not 2022.

items.q: Is 38 + 25 less than 1, exactly 1, between 1 and 2, or more than 2?
items.e: Both fractions are less than 12, so the sum is less than 12 + 12 = 1. So the answer is less than 1.

items.q: Is 56 + 47 less than 1, exactly 1, between 1 and 2, or more than 2?
items.e: Both fractions are more than 12, so the sum is more than 12 + 12 = 1. Each one is less than 1, so the sum is less than 2. So the answer is between 1 and 2.

items.q: The dot shows 0.2. Which benchmark is 0.2 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.2 is 0.2 from 0, 0.3 from 0.5 and 0.8 from 1. It is closest to 0.

items.q: The dot shows 0.9. Which benchmark is 0.9 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.9 is 0.9 from 0, 0.4 from 0.5 and 0.1 from 1. It is closest to 1.

items.q: The dot shows 0.48. Which benchmark is 0.48 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.48 is 0.48 from 0, 0.02 from 0.5 and 0.52 from 1. It is closest to 0.5. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.50.

items.q: The dot shows 0.82. Which benchmark is 0.82 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.82 is 0.82 from 0, 0.32 from 0.5 and 0.18 from 1. It is closest to 1. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.50.

items.q: Which benchmark is 0.125 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.125 is 0.125 from 0, 0.375 from 0.5 and 0.875 from 1. It is closest to 0. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.500.

items.q: Which benchmark is 0.61 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.61 is 0.61 from 0, 0.11 from 0.5 and 0.39 from 1. It is closest to 0.5. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.50.

items.q: Which benchmark is 0.875 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.875 is 0.875 from 0, 0.375 from 0.5 and 0.125 from 1. It is closest to 1. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.500.

items.q: Which benchmark is 0.37 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.37 is 0.37 from 0, 0.13 from 0.5 and 0.63 from 1. It is closest to 0.5. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.50.

items.q: Which benchmark is 0.705 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.705 is 0.705 from 0, 0.205 from 0.5 and 0.295 from 1. It is closest to 0.5. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.500.

items.q: Which benchmark is 0.16 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.16 is 0.16 from 0, 0.34 from 0.5 and 0.84 from 1. It is closest to 0. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.50.

items.q: Which benchmark is 0.064 closest to: 0, 0.5 or 1?
items.e: 0.064 is 0.064 from 0, 0.436 from 0.5 and 0.936 from 1. It is closest to 0. Tip: think of 0.5 as 0.500.

items.q: Leah says 0.09 is closest to 1 because 9 is a big digit. Is she right?
items.e: Leah is not right. The 9 is in the hundredths place, so 0.09 is only 9 hundredths. 0.09 is 0.09 from 0, 0.41 from 0.5 and 0.91 from 1. It is closest to 0.

items.q: Round 3.48 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 3.48 is between 3 and 4. The decimal part is 0.48, which is less than 0.5, so round down. Answer: 3. Do not look at the last digit (8). Compare 0.48 with 0.50.

items.q: Round 6.52 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 6.52 is between 6 and 7. The decimal part is 0.52, which is more than 0.5, so round up. Answer: 7.

items.q: Round 12.095 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 12.095 is between 12 and 13. The decimal part is 0.095, which is less than 0.5, so round down. Answer: 12. Compare 0.095 with 0.500: it is less, even though 9 is a big digit.

items.q: Round 4.38 to the nearest half (a whole number or a number ending in .5).
items.e: 4.38 is between 4 and 4.5. It is 0.38 from 4 and 0.12 from 4.5, so it is closest to 4.5.

items.q: Round 7.84 to the nearest half (a whole number or a number ending in .5).
items.e: 7.84 is between 7.5 and 8. It is 0.34 from 7.5 and 0.16 from 8, so it is closest to 8.

items.q: Which decimal is closest to 0.5?
items.e: Write them all with three decimal places and compare with 0.500: 0.47 is 0.03 away; 0.57 is 0.07 away; 0.405 is 0.095 away; 0.05 is 0.45 away. 0.47 is the closest. 0.05 is 5 hundredths, not 5 tenths.

items.q: Estimate 2.48 + 3.9. Round each decimal to the nearest half (a whole number or a number ending in .5).
items.e: Round each decimal to the nearest half: 2.5 + 4 = 6.5. (The exact answer is 6.38.)

items.q: Estimate 0.92 + 0.49 + 0.06. Round each decimal to the nearest half (a whole number or a number ending in .5).
items.e: Round each decimal to the nearest half: 1 + 0.5 + 0 = 1.5. (The exact answer is 1.47.)

items.q: Estimate 24 680 + 13 240 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest thousand: 25 000 + 13 000 = 38 000. (The exact answer is 37 920.)

items.q: Estimate 36 450 + 21 830 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest thousand: 36 000 + 22 000 = 58 000. (The exact answer is 58 280.)

items.q: Estimate 18 450 + 32 900 + 9720 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest thousand: 18 000 + 33 000 + 10 000 = 61 000. (The exact answer is 61 070.)

items.q: Estimate 48 315 + 29 780 by rounding each number to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten thousand: 50 000 + 30 000 = 80 000. (The exact answer is 78 095.)

items.q: Estimate 71 400 + 15 600 by rounding each number to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten thousand: 70 000 + 20 000 = 90 000. (The exact answer is 87 000.)

items.q: Estimate 245 800 + 312 400 by rounding each number to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten thousand: 250 000 + 310 000 = 560 000. (The exact answer is 558 200.)

items.q: Estimate 126 400 + 381 950 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest hundred thousand: 100 000 + 400 000 = 500 000. (The exact answer is 508 350.)

items.q: Estimate 452 300 + 218 700 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred thousand.
items.e: Round each number to the nearest hundred thousand: 500 000 + 200 000 = 700 000. (The exact answer is 671 000.)

items.q: Estimate 48 × 7 by rounding 48 to its greatest place.
items.e: Round 48 to its greatest place: 50 × 7 = 350. (5 × 7 = 35, then write 1 zero.) (The exact answer is 336.)

items.q: Estimate 83 × 6 by rounding 83 to its greatest place.
items.e: Round 83 to its greatest place: 80 × 6 = 480. (8 × 6 = 48, then write 1 zero.) (The exact answer is 498.)

items.q: Estimate 396 × 6 by rounding 396 to its greatest place.
items.e: Round 396 to its greatest place: 400 × 6 = 2400. (4 × 6 = 24, then write 2 zeros.) (The exact answer is 2376.)

items.q: Estimate 612 × 8 by rounding 612 to its greatest place.
items.e: Round 612 to its greatest place: 600 × 8 = 4800. (6 × 8 = 48, then write 2 zeros.) (The exact answer is 4896.)

items.q: Estimate 2875 × 4 by rounding 2875 to its greatest place.
items.e: Round 2875 to its greatest place: 3000 × 4 = 12 000. (3 × 4 = 12, then write 3 zeros.) (The exact answer is 11 500.)

items.q: Estimate 48 × 31 by rounding each number to its greatest place.
items.e: Round both numbers to their greatest place: 50 × 30 = 1500. (5 × 3 = 15, then write 2 zeros.) (The exact answer is 1488.)

items.q: Estimate 67 × 22 by rounding each number to its greatest place.
items.e: Round both numbers to their greatest place: 70 × 20 = 1400. (7 × 2 = 14, then write 2 zeros.) (The exact answer is 1474.)

items.q: Estimate 89 × 53 by rounding each number to its greatest place.
items.e: Round both numbers to their greatest place: 90 × 50 = 4500. (9 × 5 = 45, then write 2 zeros.) (The exact answer is 4717.)

items.q: Estimate 315 × 19 by rounding each number to its greatest place.
items.e: Round both numbers to their greatest place: 300 × 20 = 6000. (3 × 2 = 6, then write 3 zeros.) (The exact answer is 5985.)

items.q: Estimate 724 × 48 by rounding each number to its greatest place.
items.e: Round both numbers to their greatest place: 700 × 50 = 35 000. (7 × 5 = 35, then write 3 zeros.) (The exact answer is 34 752.)

items.q: Noah estimates 18 600 + 24 700 as 19 000 + 25 000 = 44 000. Is the exact sum more or less than 44 000?
items.e: Both numbers were rounded up (18 600 → 19 000 and 24 700 → 25 000), so the estimate is too big. The exact sum, 43 300, is less than 44 000.

items.q: Mei estimates 412 × 6 as 400 × 6 = 2400. Is the exact product more or less than 2400?
items.e: 412 was rounded down to 400, so the estimate is too small. The exact product, 2472, is more than 2400.

sets.title: Is the answer reasonable? Word problems

items.q: A school’s Terry Fox Run raises $2480 in the morning and $1365 in the afternoon. About how much money is that? Round to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: $2500 + $1400 = $3900. (The exact answer is $3845.)

items.q: A park counts 14 865 visitors on Saturday and 12 390 visitors on Sunday. About how many visitors is that? Round to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 15 000 + 12 000 = 27 000. (The exact answer is 27 255.)

items.q: A BC Ferries boat carries 372 vehicles on each trip. It makes 8 trips in one day. About how many vehicles is that? Round 372 to its greatest place.
items.e: Round to the greatest place: 400 × 8 = 3200 vehicles. (4 × 8 = 32, then write 2 zeros.) (The exact answer is 2976 vehicles.)

items.q: Grouse Mountain’s gondola carries 98 people on each trip. It makes 42 trips one morning. About how many people ride it? Round each number to its greatest place.
items.e: Round to the greatest place: 100 × 40 = 4000 people. (1 × 4 = 4, then write 3 zeros.) (The exact answer is 4116 people.)

items.q: Ryan’s school orders 23 boxes of granola bars for a field trip. Each box holds 48 bars. About how many bars is that? Round each number to its greatest place.
items.e: Round to the greatest place: 20 × 50 = 1000 bars. (2 × 5 = 10, then write 2 zeros.) (The exact answer is 1104 bars.)

items.q: The nature house in Stanley Park counts 12 865 visitors in July and 12 390 visitors in August. Simran adds them and gets 25 255. Is her answer reasonable? Round to the nearest thousand to check.
items.e: Estimate: 13 000 + 12 000 = 25 000. 25 255 is close to 25 000, so the answer is reasonable.

items.q: A Kamloops arena sells 3125 tickets each night for 6 nights. Nadia says that is 18 750 tickets. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 3000 × 6 = 18 000. 18 750 is close to 18 000, so the answer is reasonable.

items.q: A ferry carries 375 cars on each trip and makes 28 trips in a week. Liam says that is 1050 cars. Is his answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 400 × 30 = 12 000. 1050 is far from 12 000, so the answer is not reasonable. The exact answer is 10 500. Liam lost a zero.

items.q: Chloe hikes 2.48 km to a lookout and then 3.9 km to a lake in Whistler. She says she hiked 2.87 km in all. Is her answer reasonable?
c: Yes, it is close to 5 km
No, it should be about 5 km
Yes, it is close to 6.5 km
No, it should be about 6.5 km
items.e: Estimate: 2.5 + 4 = 6.5. 2.87 km is far from 6.5 km, so the answer is not reasonable. The exact answer is 6.38 km. Chloe lined up 3.9 as 0.39. Line up the decimal points.

items.q: Kai runs 78 km on Monday and 56 km on Tuesday. He adds the tops and the bottoms and says he ran 1214 km in all. Is his answer reasonable?
c: No, it should be about 2 km
Yes, it is close to 1 km
No, it should be about 1 km
Yes, it is close to 2 km
items.e: Estimate: 78 is close to 1 and 56 is close to 1, so 1 + 1 = 2. 1214 km is far from 2 km, so the answer is not reasonable. The exact answer is 11724 km. Do not add the tops and the bottoms.

items.q: A whale-watching boat in Victoria takes 64 people on each trip. It makes 38 trips in May. Use an estimate to choose the reasonable number of people.
items.e: Estimate: 60 × 40 = 2400. Only 2432 is close to 2400. 24 320 has an extra zero, 704 forgets that the 3 in 38 means 30, and 102 adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: A SkyTrain carries 386 people. 6 full trains arrive at a station. Use an estimate to choose the reasonable number of people.
items.e: Estimate: 400 × 6 = 2400. Only 2316 is close to 2400. 23 160 has an extra zero, 392 adds instead of multiplying, and 231 is missing a digit.

items.q: Harjot has $50 for lunch at Grouse Mountain. He wants a burger for $12.85, a salad for $18.40 and a smoothie for $16.95. Is $50 enough? Round to the nearest dollar.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $13 + $18 + $17 = $48. $48 is less than $50, so yes. (The exact cost is $48.20.)

items.q: The school gym has 450 chairs for the spring concert. 168 students, 145 parents and 172 grandparents are coming. Are there enough chairs? Round to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 200 + 100 + 200 = 500. 500 is more than 450, so no. (Exactly 485 people are coming.)

items.q: A bakery in Nanaimo makes 285 buns each day for 6 days. Olivia estimates 300 × 6 = 1800 buns. Is the exact number more or less than 1800?
items.e: 285 was rounded up to 300, so the estimate is too big. The exact number, 1710, is less than 1800.

items.q: Mateo’s family drives 48.6 km on the Sea-to-Sky Highway, then 12.7 km more to a campsite. About how far do they drive? Round each to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Round each one: 48.6 → 49 and 12.7 → 13. 49 + 13 = 62. (The exact distance is 61.3 km. 60 drops the decimal parts.)

items.q: Mei uses 58 cup of flour and 112 cup of sugar for pancakes. About how much is that in all? Use the benchmarks 0, 12 and 1.

items.q: Jasleen walks 1112 km to school and 49 km to the library. About how far does she walk? Use the benchmarks 0, 12 and 1.
